memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua said to the people, "You are not able to serve the Lord. He is a holy God; he is a jealous God. He will not forgive your rebellion and your sins. If you forsake the Lord and serve foreign gods, he will turn and bring disaster on you and make an end of you, after he has been good to you." — Josh 24:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua's response is startling. When the people promise to serve the Lord, he tells them, "You are not able to serve the Lord." What kind of leader discourages willing followers? A wise and honest one. Joshua wanted them to grasp the seriousness of what they were pledging. God is holy and jealous — He will not share His people's hearts with idols, and He will not treat rebellion lightly.

We should not soften these words. Joshua is confronting them with the sheer weight of God's holiness. To serve such a God, casually and in their own strength, was beyond them. He wanted no shallow, self-confident commitments made without counting the cost.

There is a deep truth here that prepares us for the gospel. In our own strength, none of us is able to serve God as He deserves. His standard is perfect holiness, and we fall short (Rom 3:23). Joshua's hard words expose our need — the very need that only Christ can meet.

This is why the good news is so good. What we could never do, God did for us in His Son. Christ served God perfectly and gives us His Spirit to enable what we could never manage alone (Phil 2:13). The right response to God's holiness is not self-confidence but a humble cry for grace. Come to God knowing you cannot serve Him on your own — and receive the help only He can give.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take the holiness of God as seriously as Joshua did?
2. Why is it important to know you cannot serve God in your own strength?
3. How does your need drive you to depend on Christ and His Spirit?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, I cannot serve You in my own strength. Thank You that in Christ You give what You require. Work in me by Your Spirit what I could never do alone. Amen.
